connection: Session 20 created ClockEntryService and demonstrated constructor injection. Session 21 now creates PayrollService and ClockEntryQueries, uses the existing repository contract, and introduces one total-hours calculation plus one ordered-history query.
objectives: Read a LINQ pipeline from source to result.
Use Where to keep completed entries and OrderByDescending to show newest entries first.
Use Sum with an inline projection to calculate total hours.
Create PayrollService with the interface dependency established in Session 20.

visuals.title: A query is a sequence of transformations
visuals.explanation: Source entries flow through filtering and ordering; each operator returns another sequence.

visuals.title: Where removes open entries
visuals.explanation: Only entries with a clock-out can safely provide a completed duration.

visuals.title: Sum projects and aggregates
visuals.explanation: The lambda converts each ClockEntry to hours; Sum combines those numbers into one total.

visuals.title: Ordering states a visible requirement
visuals.explanation: OrderByDescending on ClockIn produces newest-first history rather than relying on source insertion order.

preQuiz.prompt: Why filter open entries before calling GetDuration?
options: An open entry has no completed duration
preQuiz.explanation: The filter protects the duration invariant.

preQuiz.prompt: What does the lambda in Sum return?
options: The numeric hours for one entry
preQuiz.explanation: Sum projects each element to a number and aggregates those numbers.

preQuiz.prompt: Does OrderByDescending modify the source collection?
options: No; it returns an ordered sequence
preQuiz.explanation: LINQ query operators do not reorder the original List.

concept.title: Where filters by a requirement
paragraphs: A completed-history query excludes entries whose Clockout is null before any duration calculation.

Where returns a new IEnumerable<ClockEntry>; it does not remove anything from entries and it does not clone the ClockEntry objects. The new sequence normally contains references to the same objects. Memory anchor: New sequence. Same objects.
LINQ returns a new sequence. It does not change the source, so the returned sequence must be stored, returned, or enumerated.
The learner's current ClockEntry class spells the property Clockout, so this session uses that exact spelling.

concept.title: Sum can project and aggregate
paragraphs: PayrollService obtains completed entries through IClockEntryRepository, then maps each one to GetDuration()?.TotalHours ?? 0 inside Sum.
There is no need for a separate Select when no caller needs the intermediate sequence of numbers.

concept.title: Side note: why nullable operators appear here
paragraphs: This nullable-value detail supports the calculation, but it is not a new LINQ requirement. Read it when you want to understand the expression more deeply; then return to the main Sum example.

The learner's GetDuration method returns TimeSpan?. The ?. operator reads TotalHours only when a duration exists. The ?? operator supplies 0 when that result is null, producing the non-null double required by Sum and WorkSummary.

The repository filters out entries whose Clockout is null, and GetDuration throws for an open entry, so completed entries should normally have a duration. The nullable return signature still requires the caller to handle the type's possible null state.
If GetDuration is later corrected to return non-nullable TimeSpan because it always returns a duration or throws, the caller can use GetDuration().TotalHours directly.

concept.title: Ordering should express the caller's need
paragraphs: CompletedNewestFirst uses OrderByDescending because a history screen normally shows recent entries first.
OrderByDescending returns another IEnumerable<ClockEntry>, so the Where result can flow directly into the next operator without changing the original collection.

Without ToList, the returned pipeline normally remains deferred and runs when it is enumerated by foreach, Sum, ToList, or another terminal operation. ToList runs the query at that point and stores the results in a new List<ClockEntry>.

A List<ClockEntry> still implements IEnumerable<ClockEntry>, so more LINQ can follow ToList. The distinction is execution timing, not whether LINQ can continue. No ToList: keep the query deferred. ToList: run it now and store the results. Session 23 explores that timing in depth.

lab.objective: Create PayrollService and ClockEntryQueries, then use LINQ to calculate total hours and return completed entries newest first.
lab.startingCondition: The learner's Domain project contains Models and Services folders, uses no explicit namespace declarations, and already contains IClockEntryRepository and ClockEntryService. PayrollService and ClockEntryQueries do not exist yet.
steps: Create src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain/Services/PayrollService.cs. Do not add a namespace because the learner's existing Domain files do not declare one.
In PayrollService.cs, declare a public sealed class named PayrollService.
In PayrollService, declare a private readonly IClockEntryRepository field named _clockEntryRepository.
Add a public PayrollService constructor with an IClockEntryRepository parameter named clockEntryRepository.
In the PayrollService constructor, assign clockEntryRepository to _clockEntryRepository.

Add a public CalculateTotalHours method that returns double and accepts int employeeId, DateTime startDate, and DateTime endDate; keep the method temporarily unfinished with throw new NotImplementedException().
In CalculateTotalHours, call _clockEntryRepository.GetEmployeeClockEntries(employeeId, startDate, endDate) and store the returned sequence in a variable named entries.
Replace the temporary throw by returning entries.Sum(entry => entry.GetDuration()?.TotalHours ?? 0). Sum asks the selector for one number per entry and adds those numbers.
Create src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.Domain/Models/ClockEntryQueries.cs. Do not add a namespace because the learner's existing Domain files do not declare one.
In ClockEntryQueries.cs, declare a public static class named ClockEntryQueries.

In ClockEntryQueries, add a public static CompletedNewestFirst method that accepts IEnumerable<ClockEntry> entries, returns IEnumerable<ClockEntry>, and remains temporarily unfinished with throw new NotImplementedException().
In CompletedNewestFirst, call Where on entries, keep entries whose Clockout property is not null, and store the returned sequence in a variable named completedEntries. Where does not modify entries.
Call OrderByDescending on completedEntries, order by each entry's ClockIn property, and store the returned sequence in a variable named orderedEntries.
Replace the temporary throw by returning orderedEntries without calling ToList. No ToList keeps this query deferred; Session 23 examines when it runs.
Open src/PinkMachine19.TimeClock.App/Program.cs and preserve all earlier session code.
At the end of Program.cs, construct PayrollService by passing the existing clockEntryRepository variable to its constructor.
Call CalculateTotalHours with an employee ID, start date, and end date, then store the returned value in a variable named totalHours.
Display totalHours.
Call clockEntryRepository.GetEmployeeClockEntries with the same employee ID and date range, then store the returned sequence in a variable named entries.
Pass entries to ClockEntryQueries.CompletedNewestFirst and store the returned sequence in a variable named orderedEntries.
Use foreach to enumerate orderedEntries and display each ClockEntry object's ClockIn value.

postQuiz.prompt: Why can Sum contain entry => entry.GetDuration()?.TotalHours ?? 0?
options: Sum accepts a selector that produces the number to add
postQuiz.explanation: Projection and aggregation can be combined when the intermediate values are not needed.
?. safely accesses TotalHours and ?? supplies zero if the nullable result has no value.

postQuiz.prompt: Why does CompletedNewestFirst not call ToList?
options: The caller has not requested a snapshot
postQuiz.explanation: Session 23 will make the execution-time choice explicit.

postQuiz.prompt: What changes if OrderBy is used instead of OrderByDescending?

reflections: Which requirement does each LINQ operator represent?
When would a separate Select make the intermediate values clearer?
Why is handling the nullable duration different from filtering the ClockEntry sequence?
Why should open-entry filtering happen before duration calculation?
whatBreaks: Removing the completed-entry filter allows an open entry into code that calls GetDuration and can trigger an exception. Reversing OrderByDescending changes newest-first history to oldest-first. Adding ToList here would force materialization before Session 23 explains that choice.
summary: Session 21 creates PayrollService and ClockEntryQueries, uses Sum for completed hours, and composes Where with OrderByDescending for a deferred newest-first query. Every operator serves a visible requirement, and the lesson uses the folders and ClockEntry member names present in the learner's source.
